name: Dahi Chura Gud
subtitle: beaten rice softened in cold yogurt with jaggery, the Makar Sankranti breakfast

ingredients.note: thin poha dissolves; you need the thick flakes
loosens it if your yogurt is very thick
only if the jaggery is mild

prepNotes: Rinse the poha in a colander under cold running water for 15 seconds, then leave it to drain for 10 minutes — that soak is all the softening it gets.
Chill the yogurt properly; this dish is eaten cold and lukewarm dahi makes it heavy.
Break the jaggery into small shards rather than one lump so every mouthful gets some.

steps.text: Rinse the thick poha in a colander under cold water and shake it dry.
steps.tip: Fifteen seconds under the tap, no longer. Poha left sitting in water turns to paste.

steps.text: Let it drain and swell for 10 minutes; the flakes should be soft enough to crush between two fingers but still separate.
Whisk the chilled yogurt smooth in a large bowl with a pinch of salt.
Loosen it with the cold milk if it is stiff — you want the consistency of thin cream.
Fold the drained poha into the yogurt and leave it 5 minutes to absorb.
steps.tip: Fold, do not beat. The flakes should stay recognisable.

steps.text: Taste and stir in the sugar only if the mixture is flat.
Serve into bowls with a generous pile of jaggery shards on the side of each portion, to be broken off and eaten with each spoonful.
steps.tip: The jaggery goes alongside, not stirred in — the contrast of cold sour dahi and sharp sweet gud is the dish.

storage: Assemble and eat within an hour; the poha keeps swelling and the yogurt turns sour. Soaked poha can be drained and refrigerated for a few hours ahead, but mix in the yogurt only at the table.
